Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.,Paras Nath Rai,Pranjal Mehrotra Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Manish Kumar Nigam,J.
1.

Heard Shri Vinay Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, Shri Pranjal Mehrotra,
learned counsel appearing for respondents No. 1 & 2, Shri P.N. Rai, learned counsel for respondent No. 5.
2.

The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus commanding the respondent No. 4 i.e. Additional District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue) Kaushambi to decide the representations dated 28.11.2023 and 06.05.2024 in light of Government Order dated 12.05.2016 in Malti Shukla And 4 Others vs Union Of India And 4 Others on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20041565/
1 relation to Khasra No. 43 area 0.2000 hectare, Gram Adampur Nadir Ali Kachhar, Tehsil Chayal,
District Kaushambi and Khasra No. 954 area 0.9660 hectare, Gram Patti Narwar Upparhar, Tehsil Chayal, District Kaushambi.
3.

sentences.text: On 24.07.2024, the following order was passed:-
"1. Learned
counsel

for the respondents to obtain instructions and apprise the Court of their stand in relation to the plea of the petitioners that their additional land has been taken over by the respondents without payment of any compensation

. 
2. Put up this case as fresh on 14.08.2024."
4.

On matter being taken up today, learned standing counsel has placed on record the written instructions dated 08.08.2024 received from Competent Authority/Land Acquisition Officer,
Kaushambi.
Shri P.N. Rai, Advocate has placed on record the written instructions received from PWD, Prayagraj.
In both the instructions, the stand taken is that no excess land of the petitioners has been taken for construction of road.

Only area admeasuring 0.3978 hectare of Plot No. 954 and 0.1317 hectare of Plot No. 43 which had been acquired under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 is being utilized for construction of road.
The respondents had carried out a demarcation on the spot in presence of the petitioners.
A spot memo has been enclosed bearing signatures of the petitioners.
It clearly recites that the remaining area i.e. unacquired part of their land has been demarcated.
5. In such view of the matter, we are of the opinion that no further enquiry is required in the instant case.

6. Accordingly, the petition stands disposed of with liberty to the petitioners to avail such other remedy as may be advised in case they feel aggrieved by the demarcation exercise undertaken by the respondents.

Order Date :- 14.8.2024 Mukesh Kr.
(Manish Kumar Nigam,J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.)
